title: null writes nothing on every side (FORMA-182; DR-9 rule 5, the second half of design 4 rule 5)
contract: null and undefined write nothing. As a text child they contribute no text: the walker holds an empty dynamic range with one U+200B so the browser creates a Text node, and its visible text is empty; h() appends nothing; strict adoption expects an empty string. As an attribute value the attribute is absent on both sides, and a later null removes it. Inside a textarea or title they contribute an empty string to the composed value. A later null written into a live text range clears it to empty text. The word 'null' is never written (v1's adoption wrote it; DR-9).
consumers: crates/forma-ir/src/walker.rs > value_rule_vectors (DYN_TEXT and DYN_ATTR on a Null slot, static and dynamic textarea children)
packages/core/src/dom/__tests__/value-rule-5-null.test.ts (h() children and attributes, childText, adoption expectations and later writes; undefined beside null in every case)
packages/core/e2e/value-rules.spec.ts (the walker's ranges, composed text and textarea parsed by the three engines and strictly adopted without a write; a later null removing the attribute)
note: Hand-enumerated. JSON carries null only; the TypeScript suite runs every vector a second time with undefined in null's place, since h() treats both alike. The walker has one absent value, Null.
